previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for dizziness, shortness of breath, and chest pain. His dizziness was attributed to dehydration from a recent increase in furosemide, which resolved with IV fluids. Workup revealed significant weight loss, elevated inflammatory markers, liver enzyme abnormalities, myalgias, and a restrictive lung pattern on PFTs. After multidisciplinary evaluation, a preliminary diagnosis of amiodarone toxicity was made. Amiodarone and atorvastatin were discontinued, and a short course of prednisone was initiated for lung inflammation. He improved clinically, with stable vital signs and ambulation. Discharge planning included follow-up with pulmonology, hepatology, cardiology, and a chest CT to monitor for amiodarone-induced lung injury. He was discharged home in stable condition with clear medication instructions and outpatient appointments scheduled.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ YOM with PMH sig for DMII, CAD s/p multiple stents, ICD, dCHF 
(EF 45% ___, AVR with mechanical valve on coumadin, 
multiple strokes on coumadin and recent admission for 
dehydration and presumptive amiodarone toxicity who c/o 
nausea/vomiting (4 episodes) and watery diarrhea (4 episodes) of 
1 day duration.
.
# N/V/D - Symptoms were felt to be consistent with a viral 
gastroenteritis and perhaps his underlying hepatic pathology 
(see below). Stool studies were negative. AM cortisol was 
checked to assess for adrenal insufficiency- was within normal 
limits. He was empirically treated with flagyl and cipro for 5 
days with improvement in his diarrhea and nausea. He was 
administered anti-emetics with some effect. He was discharged 
with compazine and SL zofran and instructed to take these as 
needed, and before meals if necessary. 
.
# Elevated Liver Enzymes - Patient presented with RUQ/epigastric 
abdominal pain and elevated LFTs. CT abdomen showed gallstones 
w/o evidence of cholecystitis and no acute pathology. LFT 
abnormality was predominantly hepatocellular pattern, now with 
AST>ALT. Also with persistently elevated ESR, CRP. DDx was ASH 
vs. NASH vs. amiodarone toxicity vs. autoimmune hepatitis. Pt 
denied signnificant use of EtOH. Hepatology was consulted and 
recommended full sending autoimmune markers, ___ disease 
markers, viral panel which were notable for mildly positive 
alpha 1 anti-trypsin (211). Recommended transjugular biopsy, but 
given patient's anticoagulated status and history of strokes 
even while anticoagulated this was not pursued during this 
hospitalization. His nausea was treated as above and he was set 
up with outpatient hepatology follow up.
.
# Inflammatory condition / Weight loss - Elevated markers (ESR, 
CRP) and known weight loss. Also known polyclonal 
hypergammaglobulinemia. DDx includes various rheumatologic 
disorders including GCA, PMR, and autoimmune hepatitis. Patient 
was seen by rheumatology who felt that GCA was unlikely given 
clinical presentation and recommended optho eval, ultrasound, 
+/- temporal biopsy if suspicion should increase. 
.
# S/p CVA: Per neuro no acute neurologic abnormalities 
concerning for CVA. Pt not on plavix ___ epistaxis. Was 
continued on asa 81 mg. Coumadin was held given patient was 
supratherapeutic during hospitalization (INR increased when 
cipro started), but he was trending down on the day of d/c and 
coumadin was restarted at 7.5 mg daily.
.
# CAD: Was ruled out with two sets of negative troponins. 
Continued asa 81 mg and metoprolol 12.5 BID. Atorvastatin was 
held as per prior admission.
.
# sCHF (EF 45%): NYHA class III. Recently increased lasix dose 
for peripheral edema. Likely precipitated volume depletion and 
pre-syncope. BNP not elevated and no pulm edema on CXR. Lasix 
was initially held given fluid losses and was restarted on his 
home dose when patient tolerating POs and ___ edema was starting 
to worsen.
.
# DM: Held glyburide and put patient on insulin sliding scale.
.
# AVR/arrhythmia: INR was supratheraputic- goal 2.5-3.4. 
Coumadin was held and then restarted at discharge as above. His 
___ clinic (___ anticoag) was emailed with notification of 
his discharge and INR check was arranged for ___. Was 
continued on his home beta blocker.
.
# COPD: No active issues. Nebs were given PRN and was continued 
on home advair.

radiology_notes.text:
AP AND LATERAL CHEST ___, AT 18:46 HOURS.

HISTORY:  Multiple medical problems with recent hospitalization for amiodarone
toxicity, presenting with one-day history of nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Lung volumes remain diminished.  There is resultant bronchovascular
crowding.  Subtle engorgement of the central pulmonary vasculature is again
identified, although no frank edema is noted.  There is no focal
consolidation.  Again noted is a dual-chamber pacemaker/AICD in stable and
standard position and course from a left subclavian approach.  The median
sternotomy wires are stable.  There is marked aortic tortuosity.  The cardiac
silhouette is enlarged.  All findings are stable.  Bilateral pleural effusions
are again evident, and may have slightly enlarged since the prior examination.
Degenerative changes are seen throughout the thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:  Interval enlargement of still small bilateral pleural effusions. 
No definite pneumonia identified.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ male with right upper quadrant tenderness.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial images were acquired of the abdomen and pelvis following the
administration of intravenous contrast, and reformatted in the coronal and
sagittal planes.

FINDINGS:

LUNG BASES:  There are bilateral pleural effusions, moderate in size on the
right and small on the left with adjacent compressive atelectasis.  There is
no pericardial effusion.  Pacer leads are partially imaged.

ABDOMEN:  The liver and spleen are normal in appearance.  The pancreas and
adrenals appear normal.  There are gallstones within the gallbladder, though
there is no gallbladder wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid.  The kidneys
demonstrate symmetric contrast enhancement and brisk excretion.  Incidental
note is made of a 3.5 cm left upper pole renal cyst.  The aorta is normal in
caliber along its length with moderate atherosclerotic calcification; its
major branches appear patent.  There is no retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

The stomach is decompressed.  The duodenum is normal in appearance. 
Visualized loops of small bowel are fluid filled and prominent, but taper
normally in the more distal ileum.  The terminal ileum is normal in
appearance.

PELVIS:
The bladder is normal in appearance.  Diverticula are seen throughout the
colon from the sigmoid to the cecum.  There is no pericolic stranding to
suggest the diagnosis of diverticulitis.  Minimal thickening along the left
lateral conal fascia is chronic in nature and unchanged.

BONE WINDOWS:  No concerning lytic or blastic osseous lesions are seen.  A
sclerotic focus within the right ilium likely represents a bone island.  There
is multilevel degenerative change of the visualized spine.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Gallstones with no evidence of acute cholecystitis.

2.  There are bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left, with
adjacent compressive atelectasis.

3.  Diverticula, with no evidence of diverticulitis.

INDICATION:  Evaluation for colonic dilatation.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Two views of the abdomen were obtained.

FINDINGS:  There is a non-obstructive bowel gas pattern.  No free air is
noted.  Residual contrast is noted within the collecting system.  No
radiopaque calculi are detected.  Mild degenerative changes are visualized in
bilateral hips.  The visualized portions of the chest, CABG wires remain
intact.

IMPRESSION:
Non-obstructive gas pattern with no evidence of obstruction.
